simple.meaning: חָשַׁל (châshal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to make (intrans. be ) unsteady , i.e. weak.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Deuteronomy, beginning at Deuteronomy 25:18. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָשַׁל (H2826) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָשַׁל (châshal) / H2826 is traced through Deuteronomy 25:18 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to make (intrans. be ) unsteady , i.e. weak
definitions.full: H2826. chashal [ חָשַׁל ] verb shatter (Biblical Aramaic חֲשַׁל shatter ; Late Hebrew Pi`el, || משׁבר ; Syriac forge a metal, Arabic drive cattle violently ; Assyrian —ašâlu , shatter , destroy Zim BP 12 Dl Pr 42 ) — Niph`al Participle figurative הַנֶּחֱשָׁלִים כָּלֿ Deut 25:18 all the shattered ones , i.e. those broken down, worn out, followed by וְיָגֵעַ עָיֵף וְאַתָּה ; others think = חלשׁ .

occurrences.englishText: how he met you by the way, and struck the rearmost of you, all who were feeble behind you, when you were faint and weary; and he didn’t fear God.
